To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

“Post-partum nutrition and/or exercise interventions may result in modest weight loss compared with standard care, but there is insufficient evidence to support the effect of these interventions on metabolic risk or inflammatory biomarkers.
combined nutrition and exercise postpartum interventions can achieve modest weight loss, but the evidence is insufficient to recommend any particular postpartum intervention for weight loss.

“Combined nutrition and exercise post-partum interventions are feasible but the effect on weight loss remains uncertain. More research is needed on the effect of nutrition and exercise interventions in this setting, with particular emphasis on the duration, intensity and frequency of exercise, and the timing of the intervention.”
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of exercise and nutrition on weight, adipose tissue and metabolic risk factors in postpartum women.
the development of behavioral guidelines for postpartum weight control.
the effects of nutrition and exercise on weight loss and weight maintenance after pregnancy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
postpartum interventions can result in weight loss, but the effect is modest and there is no evidence of an impact on metabolic outcomes.
there is insufficient evidence for the effectiveness of post-partum combined interventions on weight loss, metabolic risk factors and obesity-related inflammatory biomarkers.
there is insufficient evidence to recommend or discourage post-partum weight loss interventions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the current evidence does not support the efficacy of post-partum weight loss programs.
postpartum women can lose weight through exercise or a combination of nutrition and exercise, but there is insufficient evidence to support the use of nutrition-only interventions.
the evidence for the effectiveness of combined post-partum interventions is promising, but not yet conclusive.
The main takeaway from our work is that
post-partum women are a heterogeneous population and there is no one size fits all approach.
there are no data to support the development of behavioral guidelines for weight loss in the post-partum period.
the evidence for post-partum behavioral weight control interventions is insufficient to inform clinical guidelines for weight control.
